activities.caption: pair each market precondition with its state-backed provider
activities.name: peMarketMatch

config.prompt: What every transaction runs on — pair each precondition with what supplies it:

pairs.right: someone with coercive power defines ownership and defends it
standardised weights, company law, insolvency rules

config.why: Markets are not self-creating — every transaction runs on state-supplied rules, and the quality of those rules is the deep variable in development.

activities.caption: bet the magnitude — the sugar program's consumer bill
activities.name: peSugarEstimate

config.prompt: Per the worked example: what does the US sugar program cost consumers per year?
config.why: Roughly 3–4 billion dollars a year — call it $10–15 per household — against tens of thousands of dollars per year for a few thousand growers. Per household, fighting it is never worth the stamp; per grower, it is the best investment in the portfolio.
config.context: $3–4 billion a year, about $10–15 per household

activities.caption: file each institutional piece under its capitalist variety
activities.name: peVarietiesSort

config.prompt: Liberal versus coordinated market economies — file each piece:

items.label: competitive advantage in radical innovation and fast reallocation
patient bank finance, long employment tenures
competitive advantage in incremental innovation and deep workforce skills

config.why: The pieces cohere through institutional complementarity — which is why transplants fail: copying Silicon Valley requires the whole liberal ecosystem, not the office parks.

activities.anchor: Historically the arrow runs the other way
activities.caption: bet on where impersonal markets come from
activities.name: peArrowPredict

config.q: Is the free market the natural state of the economy, with regulation the intrusion?
choices: yes — markets predate states and regulation arrives later
no — impersonal markets are institutional achievements that took centuries and states to build
only in the twentieth century did states create markets
the question is unanswerable either way
config.why: Every performance difference between rich countries is institutional difference — the Nordics and the US are both overwhelmingly market economies whose divergent outcomes trace to rule choices, not more versus less market.

activities.anchor: East Asia forced the century's biggest revision
activities.caption: rebuild the developmental-state playbook in order
activities.name: peDevOrder

config.prompt: The East Asian route, in the order the discipline runs it — assemble the playbook:
items: State picks winners with directed credit at near-zero real rates
Infant industries get protection while they are young
The crucial discipline: export performance as the condition — subsidies continue only for firms that sell abroad and meet world prices
State picks face market tests and capital faces state tests
The debate is redefined: not 'state versus market' but which state-market interfaces, for which development stage
config.why: Discipline runs in both directions — what those states avoided was not intervention but undisciplined intervention, a lesson about design rather than a licence for slogans.

activities.caption: one line of this capture briefing is wrong
activities.name: peCaptureSpot

config.prompt: One line of this student's capture briefing is wrong — click it:
lines: Regulators know less than regulatees, so audits, whistleblower protections and mandatory disclosure carry real weight.
Capture operates through the Olson arithmetic plus revolving doors plus information dependence.
The mature literature's finding: capture is partial, variable and design-sensitive — independent agencies resist it better.
Basel II's risk-weighting delegated measurement to the regulated, with 2008 as the audited result.
Capture means the regulator has been bribed, so honesty in office is the structural cure.
config.correction: Capture operates through entirely legal channels — the regulated supply the expertise and the evidence — so structural design features (independence, disclosure, multi-stakeholder procedure) do the work good intentions cannot.
config.why: The worked case: banks' concentrated stakes versus diffuse depositor interests produced decades of under-capitalisation, with each repair round's dilution traceable in the lobbying record.

activities.anchor: Inequality is the field's integrative variable
activities.caption: drag the divider — market income versus disposable income
activities.name: peIneqCompare

config.prompt: Drag the divider — the two distributions the OECD compares:

before.label: market income
before.text: The pre-tax distribution that institutions set: labour law, minimum wages, union density — the compression effects are large and comparative.

after.label: disposable income
after.text: After tax-and-transfer redistribution — the welfare states' arithmetic made visible: similar market incomes, divergent disposable outcomes.

config.why: Inequality is jointly produced — and it is an input too: it reshapes who organises, who votes, and what the next round of rules will be.
